- domains
	* speech and language  
	* motor  
	* social-emotional  
	* cognitive  
* risk factors
	* biological  
	  * prematurity  ( NICU can follow up)
	  * low birth weight  
	  * birth injury  
	  * vision/hearing impairment  
	  * chronic illness  
	* environmental  
	  * family factors  
	    * low parental education  
	    * parental mental illness  
	    * social isolation  
	    * poverty  
	  * community factors  
	    * poor housing  
	    * poor services  
	    * limited access to care  
	* clustering  
	  * poverty \+ associated risks  
	    * strongest link to mild–moderate delay

  * mild–moderate delay  
      * kindergarten  
      * school  
  * first to suspect delay
	  * parents
* normal vs concern
	*  single delayed milestone → may be normal  
	* multiple delays → ↑ concern
* judgement capacity
	* more experience → better judgment  
    * true for organic conditions  
    * not proven for developmental problems  



- **developmental screening tests**
	* definition  
	  * standardised tools to assess developmental risk  
	* examples  
	  * Denver Developmental Screening Test (DDST)  
	    * now not used
	    * dynamic growth, one time assessment not recommended
* tool  
  * Parents’ Evaluation of Developmental Status (PEDS)  
    * 10-item questionnaire  
    * age range: birth to 8 years  
- **assessment**
	* indication  
	  * suspected developmental delay  
	* initial evaluation  
	  * paediatrician  
	    * detailed history  
	    * physical examination  
	    * neurological examination  
	    * assess aetiology  
	* investigations  
	  * based on suspicion  
	    * chromosomal  
	    * metabolic  
	    * chemical  
	    * neurological  
	* additional specialists  
	  * psychologist  
	    * cognitive testing  
	    * baseline \+ future comparison  
	  * others (as needed)  
	    * neurology  
	    * speech pathology  
	    * occupational therapy  
	    * physiotherapy  
	    * ophthalmology  
	    * social work  
	    * genetics  
	* goal  
	  * define developmental profile  
	    * strengths \+ weaknesses  
	  * identify risk factors  
	* outcome  
	  * individualised intervention plan
	
-  referal indications

	* developmental regression  
	  * loss of previously acquired skills  
	* prematurity  
	  * \<28 weeks gestation  
	  * birth weight \<1500 g  
	  * not in follow-up → refer  
	* high-risk conditions  
	  * chromosomal abnormalities  
	  * significant hearing/vision impairment  
	  * dysmorphism  
	  * abnormal neurological exam  
	* clinical concern  
	  * abnormal observations  
	  * failed screening tests  
	  * major psychosocial risk factors  
	* parental concern  
	  * persistent/major concern even if exam normal  
	* suspicion of autism  
	* referral network  
	  * paediatricians  
	  * speech therapists  
	  * psychologists  
	  * occupational therapists  
	  * early linkage → better outcomes 

## **early detection of abnormal development – GP strategy**
  * identify major risk factors  
    * regression  
    * extreme prematurity  
    * neurological abnormalities  
    * vision/hearing impairment  
  * presence of major risk 
	  * consider early referral  
  * focus areas  
    * vision  
    * hearing  
* parental concerns  
  * actively elicit concerns  
    * informal questioning  
    * formal tools (e.g. PEDS)  
  * review responses  
  * borderline findings  
    * may clarify on repeat assessment  
* referral  
  * early referral if  
    * definite developmental delay  
    * high risk for delay  
  * ensures timely formal assessment

## **childhood milestones 0–5 years**

### **communication and language milestones**

| milestone                      | average age  |
| ------------------------------ | ------------ |
| social smile                   | 6 weeks      |
| cooing                         | 3 months     |
| turns to voice                 | 4 months     |
| babbles                        | 6–9 months   |
| ‘mamma’/’dadda’ (no meaning)   | 8–9 months   |
| ‘mamma’/’dadda’ (with meaning) | 10–18 months |
| understands several words      | 1 year       |
| speaks single words            | 12–15 months |
| points to body parts           | 14–22 months |
| able to name one body part     | 18 months    |
| combines two words             | 14–24 months |
| speaks six or more words       | 12–20 months |
| able to name five body parts   | 2 years      |
| has 50 word vocabulary         | 2 years      |
| uses pronouns (me, you, I)     | 2 years      |

### **developmental milestones (tasks)**

| milestone | average age |
| ----- | ----- |
| follows eyes past midline | 6 weeks |
| smiles | 6 weeks |
| bears weight on legs (with support) | 3–7 months |
| sits with support | 4–6 months |
| sits without support | 5–8 months |
| crawls | 6–9 months |
| puts everything into mouth | 4–8 months |
| pulls to standing | 6–10 months |
| first tooth | 6–9 months |
| walks holding on | 7–13 months |
| drinks from cup | 10–15 months |
| waves goodbye | 8–12 months |
| climbs stairs | 14–20 months |
| scribbles | 1–2 years |
| uses a spoon | 14–24 months |
| puts on clothing | 21–26 months |
| jumps on spot | 20–30 months |
| rides a tricycle | 21–36 months |
| turns pages | 2 years |
| buttons up | 30–42 months |
| bowel control | 18 months – 4 years |
| bladder control (day) | 8 months – 4 years |
| clear hand preference | 2–5 years |
